title: A variational inequality for the mean of a random variable
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $f, X : \Omega \to \bbr$, and let $t \in \bbr$. Suppose that $f \ge 0$ pointwise, that $\int_\Omega f\,d\mu = 1$, and that $f$, the map $x \mapsto f(x)\log f(x) - f(x) + 1$, the map $x \mapsto e^{tX(x)}$, and the product $fX$ are all $\mu$-integrable. Writing $\Lambda(t) = \log \int_\Omega e^{tX}\,d\mu$ for the cumulant generating function of $X$ under $\mu$, one has
\[
  t \int_\Omega f(x)\,X(x)\,d\mu(x) \;\le\; \int_\Omega \bigl(f(x)\log f(x) - f(x) + 1\bigr)\,d\mu(x) + \Lambda(t).
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ is a probability measure on Ω
f, X : Ω → ℝ and t ∈ ℝ
x ↦ f(x)log f(x) − f(x) + 1 is integrable
